conditions: Windows, installed Chrome headless at 390x844 touch, next start production build, owned loopback PostgreSQL 17.11 disposable cluster, schema-only fixture, real Better Auth email OTP to a loopback stand-in, seeded professional and three services rows, no route interception

steps.name: a real client signs in on the disposable cluster
a professional with three packages is seeded into the cluster
the picker opens on a phone viewport with search, sort, chips and a count line
the category chip narrows the list to the three seeded packages
the card label and the order agree under every sort
search narrows the list and the status line counts what is left
a chosen package stays chosen when the filters change
the picker journey adds no client-side errors

samples.statusLine: 47 of 47 services shown. Your selection stays when you change filters.
3 of 47 services shown. Your selection stays when you change filters.

samples.emptyMessage: No service matched that search. Try a shorter word or another category.

notes: the three packages are real rows in services (workspace_id set, is_active true) behind a professional identity_workspaces row, so the list comes from the same join the app uses (lib/plan-repository.ts options()) rather than a mock: tests/browser/plan-v2.cjs intercepts responses and never drives these controls.

the unpriced row is seeded with price -5.00 because services.price is DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL. The served payload carries it as price: null (the repository refuses to list a figure below zero), which is why the before run of this suite is the picker without controls at all: with a normalised null arriving over HTTP, the pre-29f54bd card and the post-fix card print the same words for the same payload. The label/order divergence that 29f54bd removed is reproduced at contract level in tests/plan-catalogue-controls.cjs, and the agreement invariant is re-asserted here from the served payload rather than claimed.

quantities are read off the painted page: card order, the price string in the third span, the count in the status paragraph, the All chip, and aria-pressed. Amounts are parsed from the printed label, so a change to the currency format shows up as an order failure rather than a string mismatch.
viewport 390x844 in installed Chrome with touch emulation. This is a simulated phone, not a hand-held device, so it does not close the real-device sign-off in FND-01.

nothing off loopback is reached: the route filter aborts every request whose host is not 127.0.0.1 or localhost, the database is a disposable cluster this run creates and drops, and the OTP goes to a loopback stand-in.
